OpenAI just let businesses claim their profile in ChatGPT and build a Business Agent that answers customer questions.

Your customers are about to ask an AI about you before they ever open your website.

So the real question for every org isn't "should we build an agent?"

It's "who owns what the agent says about us?"

Copilot Studio people, you already know this meeting.

hits.draft_en:
MAI-Transcribe-2: $0.10 per hour of audio.

That's 10 cents to turn a one hour status meeting into something searchable.

Which is more than most of those meetings were worth.

I'm kidding. Mostly.

Real talk: cheap, fast transcription is the boring piece that makes the exciting agent work. Every agent you build is only as good as the context you can actually feed it.

hits.name: OpenAI Newsroom
hits.hook: OpenAINewsroom: Advanced and Standard voice retire Dec 11, virtually everyone already uses GPT-Live
hits.text:
We’re retiring Advanced and Standard voice from ChatGPT Voice on December 11, 2026.

In July, we introduced GPT-Live, our latest voice model that combines natural conversation with frontier intelligence. Since then, voice usage has nearly doubled, and virtually all people using voice in ChatGPT now use GPT-Live. This change will allow us to simplify the voice experience and focus on improving GPT-Live.

We've learned a lot from how people used both Advanced and Standard voice, and we're bringing those learnings into GPT-Live as we continue to improve areas like the depth and detail of responses, maintaining continuity across conversations, and better personalization. Our ultimate goal is to make voice a seamless part of the ChatGPT experience.

Live video and screen-sharing will continue to be powered by Advanced voice until GPT-Live has this capability.

https://t.co/B1VHs24iU1

hits.draft_en:
OpenAI is retiring the old ChatGPT voice modes on Dec 11 because virtually everyone already moved to GPT-Live.

That's the cleanest way to retire anything.

You don't kill the legacy Power App with an angry email.

You ship something better, watch usage move, and switch off the old one when nobody's left to notice.
hits.video_tip: Vertical 10s: a usage chart where the old app's line drops to zero while the new one climbs, then you calmly click 'Turn off'. Caption: 'Nobody noticed. That is the goal.'

Nine engineers. 1,211 pull requests in one day. That's the Copilot Cowork team.

I don't read that as "agents write all the code now."

I read it as: writing code stopped being the bottleneck.

Reviewing it, testing it and knowing what you're shipping is the job now.

Same thing is coming to Power Platform. More makers, more agents, more solutions. Your ALM had better be ready.

drafts.text:
OpenAI just let businesses claim their profile in ChatGPT and build a Business Agent that answers customer questions.

Your customers are about to ask an AI about you before they ever open your website.

So the real question for every org isn't "should we build an agent?"

It's "who owns what the agent says about us?"

Copilot Studio people, you already know this meeting.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 12s: phone screen typing 'Is this place open Sunday?' into ChatGPT, an agent answers confidently, then cut to you at a desk holding a sticky note that says 'Owner: ???'. Caption: 'Who owns the answer?'

drafts.text:
MAI-Transcribe-2: $0.10 per hour of audio.

That's 10 cents to turn a one hour status meeting into something searchable.

Which is more than most of those meetings were worth.

I'm kidding. Mostly.

Real talk: cheap, fast transcription is the boring piece that makes the exciting agent work. Every agent you build is only as good as the context you can actually feed it.
drafts.video_tip: Screen 10s: a calendar full of back-to-back meetings, then a counter ticking '$0.10' per block as each turns into a transcript. End on a Copilot Studio knowledge source list. Caption: '10 cents an hour'.

drafts.rides: @msdev Copilot Cowork, 1,211 PRs in a day (17,531) + your Cowork Rust post format
drafts.text:
Nine engineers. 1,211 pull requests in one day. That's the Copilot Cowork team.

I don't read that as "agents write all the code now."

I read it as: writing code stopped being the bottleneck.

Reviewing it, testing it and knowing what you're shipping is the job now.

Same thing is coming to Power Platform. More makers, more agents, more solutions. Your ALM had better be ready.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head 15s with a PR counter racing from 0 to 1,211 in the corner, then freeze on a single 'Review requested' notification. Caption: 'Who reviews 1,211?'

drafts.rides: @github Fable 5.2 (65,611) + Gemini 4 Carbon (38,370) GA in Copilot, @Azure right-size the model (8,782)
drafts.text:
Two new frontier models went GA in GitHub Copilot in about 24 hours. Fable 5.2, then Gemini 4 Carbon.

My rule for picking a model for a Copilot Studio agent hasn't changed:

Start with the smaller one.
Prove it fails.
Then upgrade.

The biggest model is not a strategy. It's a bill.
drafts.video_tip: Screen 12s: open a model picker, the list keeps growing as you scroll, you pick the smallest one, run a test that passes, then show a credit meter barely moving. Caption: 'Prove it fails first'.

drafts.rides: @OpenAINewsroom Advanced and Standard voice retired Dec 11 (324,649)
drafts.text:
OpenAI is retiring the old ChatGPT voice modes on Dec 11 because virtually everyone already moved to GPT-Live.

That's the cleanest way to retire anything.

You don't kill the legacy Power App with an angry email.

You ship something better, watch usage move, and switch off the old one when nobody's left to notice.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 10s: a usage chart where the old app's line drops to zero while the new one climbs, then you calmly click 'Turn off'. Caption: 'Nobody noticed. That is the goal.'
